correctness.rationale: Each successful extinction excursion has n-1 rare downward moves; its order-specific probability has a positive leading product of inverse occupied-set edge cuts. Summation gives success Z/(n lambda^(n-1)), with trajectories having extra upward moves of one additional inverse-lambda order. Renewal gives mean lambda^(n-1)/Z. Order chambers give an exact gap integral; changing to edge increments factorizes trees, and Laplace convolution evaluates cycles. Correct boundaries n>=2, connected simple graph, fixed n, lambda tending to infinity; 1,441 tree and 238 unicyclic exact subset-recursion checks and 6 independent CTMC rational solves pass. Scientific claims rely on proof, not the finite tests.

value.rationale: The result resolves an ecologically motivated sharp large-rescue persistence invariant and detects a surprising complete insensitivity to topology for every n-vertex tree. The strict cycle-length-only gain provides a natural, interpretable and nontrivial classification for unicyclic dispersal networks, converting empirical small-graph SIS prefactors into exact all-size values. The graph-cut integral is structurally useful beyond the displayed families; no real-world management claim or finite-rate ordering is inferred.
